newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador delays sale of telephone firm.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador delays sale of telephone firm.

text.p: Ecuador Tuesday officially postponed the sale of a stake in state telephone firm Empresa Estatal de Telecomunicaciones (Emetel) until mid-October.

"The National Modernization Council has agreed with the president of the budget committee of Congress to put off for 45 days the deadline to receive new international bids for 35 percent of Emetel shares," a council statement said.

The head of the budget committee, Alvaro Perez, said Monday he recommended delaying the sale to amend the present privatizations law. The changes introduced would allow one international operator to run both companies into which Emetel will be split, Andinatel and Pacifictel.
The sale had been due September 16 and three foreign companies -- Italy's Stet SpA, Spain's Telefonica de Espana and GTE Corp of the U.S. -- qualified as bidders.
The government says Emetel is worth about $1.2 billion.
